[element-related-term]
=== `<related-term>` Related Terms

A term that is related to the <<element-term,`<term>`>> that is being described inside a <<element-term-display,`<term-display>`>>. The related term may be a synonym, see or see also relationship, etc.

#### Usage/Remarks
The type of relationship between the term being defined and the related term is described using the <<attribute-related-term-type,`@related-term-type`>> attribute, for example, the related term is a “`synonym`”.
##### Custom Related Term Type (<<attribute-related-term-type,`@related-term-type`>>)

The <<attribute-related-term-type,`@related-term-type`>> attribute describes the relationship of the related term to the term being defined (for example, “`acronym`”, “`synonym`”, or “`translation`”). <<attribute-related-term-type,`@related-term-type`>> has as its values a fixed list of relationships. If your term relationship is not one of the listed types, you can use <<attribute-custom-type,`@custom-type`>> to describe the actual type. Set the value of <<attribute-related-term-type,`@related-term-type`>> to “`custom`” and also use <<attribute-custom-type,`@custom-type`>> to name the relationship you require. For example:
[source,xml]
....
<related-term related-term-type="custom"  
     custom-type="homonym"...>...</related-term>
....

#### Attributes

* <<attribute-custom-type,`@custom-type`>>
* <<attribute-related-term-type,`@related-term-type`>> (REQUIRED)
* <<attribute-rid,`@rid`>>
* <<attribute-specific-use,`@specific-use`>>
#### Base Attributes

* <<attribute-id,`@id`>>
* <<attribute-xml-base,`@xml:base`>>
* <<attribute-xml-lang,`@xml:lang`>> (default = en)

#### Models and Context

#### May be contained in

<<element-term-display,`<term-display>`>>, <<element-term-display-string,`<term-display-string>`>>

#### Tagged Sample

##### Part of term-display
[source,xml]
....
...
<body>
 ...
 <term-sec id="sec_2.2.5">
  <label>2.2.5</label>
  <tbx:termEntry xmlns:tbx="urn:iso:std:iso:30042:ed-1" id="term_2.2.5">...</tbx:termEntry>
  <term-display id="h2238-33">
   <term>hoogwerker</term>
   <part-of-speech norm-part-of-speech="noun">noun</part-of-speech>
   <related-term related-term-type="acronym" rid="h2238-33.a">HW</related-term>
   <def>
    <p>hefplatform bestaande uit een werkplatform en 
     een hydraulische hefinrichting gemonteerd op een zelfaangedreven 
     chassis</p>
   </def>
   <non-normative-note>
    <p>Zie <std><std-ref>EN 1777</std-ref></std>.</p>
   </non-normative-note>
  </term-display>
 </term-sec>
</body>
...
....
